name: Cafe Sissu
why_it_matters: Currently the highest-rated eatery in Sissu (#1 of 5 on Tripadvisor, 4.8/5 as of 2026), located near the Raja Ghepan temple. The dining room is properly fitted out — warm interiors, full table service — which is rare on the Lahaul side of the Atal Tunnel. The kitchen runs 10am to 11pm daily, longer than almost anywhere else in the village.
insider_tip: Reviewers flag the food as slightly overpriced for Lahaul — go for the pizza, cappuccino, or a cheesecake slice rather than full meals. In low season (Nov-Mar) it's one of the only cafes still running full service when neighbouring places are closed or skeleton-staffed.
signature_address: Near Raja Ghepan Temple, Sissu, Lahaul and Spiti District, Himachal Pradesh 175140

name: Lapiti Cafe & Stay
signature_dish: tandoori platter with Chenab valley view
why_it_matters: First eatery you hit emerging from the Atal Tunnel north portal — 250 metres on the Sissu side. Mountain views over the Chenab valley, in-house tandoor, and a 5/5 Tripadvisor rating across 8 reviews. The owner is locally known for helping travellers stranded in tunnel closures.
insider_tip: If the Atal Tunnel closes mid-trip due to snow or maintenance (not uncommon Nov-Apr), this is the closest place to wait it out with hot food and a wood heater. Call ahead on weekends — they're tight on covers and Manali day-trippers fill them up by lunch.
signature_address: 250m opposite North Portal, Atal Tunnel, Sissu, Lahaul and Spiti District 175140

name: Cafe Alpenglow
why_it_matters: One of Sissu's broader-menu cafes — Continental, Israeli (shakshuka), Chinese, Indian — set in Shooling village a short drive from the lake. 8am-midnight operating window is unusual for Lahaul, where most kitchens shut by 9pm. Reviews single out white sauce pasta and French toast.
insider_tip: The Israeli backpacker influence on the menu (shakshuka, hummus) reflects Sissu's role as a Manali alternative for the post-tunnel circuit. WiFi is free and reliable enough to actually work from — uncommon on this stretch.
signature_address: Vill. Shooling, Sissu, Lahaul and Spiti District 175131

name: Hobknob Stay & Cafe
why_it_matters: Boutique homestay-cafe combination tied to the Hobknob brand (also runs Hobknob Mountain Top in the same area). Tripadvisor + Google travel listings + active Instagram (@hobknob.experience) confirm it's currently operating. Reviewers consistently use the word 'homely' for the food — the kitchen runs as a home kitchen, not a full menu.
insider_tip: Cafe is primarily set up for in-house guests; non-residents should call ahead. The lounge is the warmest space in Sissu after dark — order a chai and sit in front of the bukhari while the temperature drops.
signature_address: Hobknob Sissu, Sissu village, Lahaul and Spiti District 175140

name: Sissu Rasoi
signature_dish: fresh paranthas with curd and pickle
why_it_matters: Small dhaba-style kitchen in Sissu village — the budget end of the spectrum after the tunnel. 11am-9pm hours, fresh-cooked Indian basics, the only Sissu place where reviews specifically call out 'reasonable rates'. Run by a family team (one server, Vinod, named in the only Tripadvisor review).
insider_tip: If the cafe-strip prices feel inflated post-Atal-Tunnel, walk inside the village to here. Order parantha-curd-pickle as the breakfast set — same combo Lahaul drivers eat before continuing to Keylong.
signature_address: Sissu Village, Lahaul and Spiti District 175140
